results.title: Data Governance for Synthetic Data | by James Fahey | Medium
results.content: # Data Governance for Synthetic Data. Synthetic data is no longer a side experiment — it’s becoming foundational to enterprise AI. • Augment sparse datasets in domains like fraud detection or rare disease research. • Preserve privacy by generating shareable data that mimics real-world distributions without exposing sensitive information. • Train specialized models where labeled real-world data is too expensive, risky, or scarce. But without proper governance, synthetic data introduces as many risks as it solves. The Five Pillars of Synthetic Data Governance. Synthetic data must be traceable back to its origins. • Which real datasets contributed to generation. • Parameters, seeds, and synthetic transformations. Maintaining audit trails ensures that regulators (HIPAA, GDPR, financial auditors) can validate claims about what went into synthetic data. Synthetic data doesn’t automatically fix bias; in fact, it can amplify systemic biases from source datasets. • Apply fairness and representation checks to synthetic datasets. • Compare distributional properties (e.g., gender, ethnicity, income bands) with real-world baselines. • Run synthetic data through bias detection pipelines similar to those used for real-world data. This ensures models trained on synthetic data don’t inadvertently worsen equity gaps. Even when data is synthetic, risks of re-identification exist if real-world signals bleed through. • k-anonymity to ensure generated records are indistinguishable from at least k-1 others. • Regular penetration testing against synthetic datasets to confirm resilience to membership inference attacks. Done right, synthetic data should be non-identifiable by design. Synthetic data must be treated with the same rigor as real data:. • Versioning: Keep track of which synthetic dataset was used for each training run. • Labeling: Mark datasets clearly as synthetic vs. • Expiration: Retire or regenerate synthetic datasets when base models, business requirements, or compliance rules change. • ISO/IEC JTC 1: Expanding existing AI standards to cover synthetic data provenance, auditability, and fairness. • NIST: Developing U.S. federal guidelines on privacy and quality assurance for synthetic data. With the right governance, synthetic data becomes a strategic enabler:. • Healthcare: Training AI on rare diseases without exposing patient records. • Finance: Simulating fraud scenarios that don’t exist in sufficient volume in real-world data. The lesson: synthetic data is not a shortcut — it’s a regulated asset.

results.title: ML Reproducibility Tools and Best Practices | A minimal Hugo website
results.content: A recurrent challenge in machine learning research is to ensure that the presented and published results are reliable, robust, and reproducible [4,5,6,7]. Reproducibility, obtaining similar results as presented in a paper using the same code and data, is necessary to verify the reliability of research findings. Pytorch Lightning provides a great way to log all hyperparameters in `.csv` files in the experiment output folder, allowing for better reproducibility. Managing your model checkpoints is very important in terms of reproducibility, as it allows you to release trained models for the community to easily verify your work, as well as build upon it. Probably the most important aspect of the exact reproducibility of your research is the seed of the experiment. Before beginning your experiments, randomly draw \(n\) seeds and set them aside in your config file, and report all experimental results aggregated over those \(n\) seeds. A higher bar of reproducibility is to report the results on *multiple datasets* to highlight the robustness of your model.

results.title: AI governance framework to be released by September 28, says Vaishnaw | Tech News - Business Standard
results.content: Home / Technology / Tech News / AI governance framework to be released by September 28, says Vaishnaw. # AI governance framework to be released by September 28, says Vaishnaw. The minister further said India will place strong emphasis on AI safety even at the AI Impact Summit it will host in February 2026, and supports the formation of a common global governance framework for AI, that is consensus-based. The government will release an Artificial Intelligence governance framework by September 28 that would define safety boundaries to safeguard citizens from AI harm, and outline checks and balances, IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said on Thursday, but added that the framework would not be "prescriptive". The minister further said India will place strong emphasis on AI safety even at the AI Impact Summit it will host in February 2026, and supports the formation of a common global governance framework for AI, that is consensus-based. The AI Impact Summit 2026 to be held in India on February 19-20, 2026, will be inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. "As we approach the AI Impact Summit, we would also like to present an AI Governance framework. The AI governance framework that will be released on September 28 will not be "prescriptive", the minister emphasised. Responding to a query on the AI-generated video depicting Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his late mother, and the measures being taken by the Government to curb such misuse, the minister said that synthetic content and deepfakes created through AI are emerging as a major challenge for society. on what kind of problem can arise from AI-generated synthetic content and deepfakes, and so the AI governance framework and the upcoming AI Impact Summit 2026, will have a big focus on AI safety, safety of citizens and users," Vaishnaw said. On what the ensuing AI governance framework would entail, Vaishnaw said it would be aimed at safeguarding citizens from AI harm. "The boundaries in which AI safety related items should be placed will be clearly defined...If there is a harm coming to a person, how should we deal with it...as we go into development of AI application and more rapid adoption of AI how do we ensure that proper checks and balances are there...that kind of framework," he explained.

results.title: GitHub - adobe-research/ProcMatRL
results.content: MatFormer is a generative model for procedural materials in Adobe Substance 3D Designer, with a primary focus on image-conditioned material graph generation. This repository contains the source code for training and evaluating a conditional MatFormer as described in the "*Procedural Material Generation with Reinforcement Learning*" paper (Li et al., SIGGRAPH Asia 2024). Our dataset and pre-trained model used for producing the results in the paper can not be released under Adobe's policy. As an alternative, we will release the pre-trained and RL-fine-tuned weights of a sample model trained using published materials in DiffMat. Please stay tuned for further updates. As outlined in the SIGGRAPH Asia paper, the training process of a conditional MatFormer for node parameter prediction involves two stages: **supervised pre-training** and **RL fine-tuning**. Then, modify `configs/train_param_generator.json` as follows:. If you need to alter the remaining command line options, please refer to their definitions in `matformer/train_param_generator.py`. The following command initiates pre-training:. python -m matformer.train_param_generator --config configs/train_param_generator.json. To fine-tune the pre-trained model using synthetic images only, modify `configs/train_ppo.json` as follows:. The remaining command line options are defined in `matformer/train_ppo.py`. python -m matformer.train_ppo --config configs/train_ppo.json. Alternatively, you can fine-tune the pre-trained model using a combination of synthetic and real images. Simply modify `configs/train_ppo_real.json` instead following the same instructions as above. python -m matformer.train_ppo --config configs/train_ppo_real.json. Similar to training, the inference procedure also comprises several steps including parameter prediction, material rendering, image-space metric calculation, and differentiable post-optimization. We have consolidated this workflow into a unified script `matformer/eval_graph_generator.py`, which is invoked likewise using a JSON configuration file. The `configs/` folder contains two starter JSON configuration files for inference, where `eval_ppo.json` uses synthetic test images and `eval_ppo_real.json` uses real test images. The result folder will be organized as the following if you set up training and inference according to the instructions above. /path/to/result ├── eval/ # Inference results │   ├── ppo_param_generator_real/ │   │   └── images/ │   │   ├── 0_xxx/ # Generated and optimized materials for each input image │   │   ├── 1_xxx/ │   │   ├── 2_xxx/ │   │   └── ... │   └── results/ # Side-by-side visual comparison figures ├── finetune/ │   └── ppo/ │   └── ppo_param_generator_real/ # RL fine-tuning checkpoints └── pretrain/ └── models/ └── param_generator/ # Supervised pre-training checkpoints.
